cases.requirement: Mutable repository membership is discovered from current approved sources and recorded as a timestamped snapshot.
cases.failure: A fixed source array is described as the complete current estate.

cases.requirement: Pagination, permissions, connector availability, local-only sources, and observation time are recorded.
cases.failure: A bounded or partial census is labeled complete.

cases.requirement: Aliases, renames, forks, mirrors, backups, generated children, and predecessor/successor records are reconciled before counts and claims are emitted.
cases.failure: Duplicate identities inflate repository, capability, or proof totals.

cases.requirement: Visibility, provenance, activity, maturity, evidence, promotion, privacy, and freshness remain separate fields.
cases.failure: One status label silently implies unrelated dimensions.

cases.requirement: The owning repository is opened before runtime, build, test, integration, or deployment claims are made.
cases.failure: Monolith catalog metadata is treated as operational proof.

cases.requirement: The latest canonical checkpoint, prior package, registry, audit, or receipt is located before new architecture or duplicate artifacts are created.
cases.failure: Existing verified work is replaced by a parallel rebuild without a controlling defect.

cases.requirement: A repository-scale mission resolves to the minimum complete subgraph plus an explicit impact perimeter.
cases.failure: The system either ignores relevant dependencies or expands into an unbounded estate sweep.

cases.requirement: Each repository uses stack-native install, static, build, test, integration, security, and deployment commands discovered from source.
cases.failure: A generic command or zero-test exit code is treated as proof.

cases.requirement: Concurrent tasks are independent by files, state, dependencies, and release surface.
cases.failure: Parallel writes race on shared state or produce unplanned merge conflicts.

cases.requirement: Repository, deep-inspection, concurrency, timeout, network, mutation, retry, and artifact budgets are declared.
cases.failure: A large run has no bounded cost or stopping condition.

cases.requirement: Deep inspection prioritizes foundations, critical paths, public flagships, shared dependencies, recent changes, failures, contradictions, security, identity collisions, and high-centrality donors.
cases.failure: Attention is distributed uniformly regardless of mission relevance and risk.

cases.requirement: Presence, documentation, static analysis, build, test, integration, and deployment remain distinct evidence levels.
cases.failure: Lower evidence is promoted into a higher claim.

cases.requirement: A required failed or blocked repository keeps the relevant wave and aggregate gate failed or blocked.
cases.failure: Many passing repositories average away one required failure.

cases.requirement: Conflicting manifests, receipts, website claims, README statements, aliases, and deployment revisions are resolved or carried visibly.
cases.failure: The newest or most convenient source silently erases a material contradiction.

cases.requirement: Generated catalogs, APIs, graph edges, backlinks, and website projections enforce the public allowlist.
cases.failure: Sensitive material is reachable through a secondary generated surface.

cases.requirement: Aggregate results state repositories discovered, considered, deeply inspected, passed, failed, blocked, excluded, and unavailable.
cases.failure: A success percentage lacks a meaningful denominator or hides exclusions.

cases.requirement: Catalog, domains, foundations, status boards, website projections, and receipts regenerate from the same reconciled state.
cases.failure: Generated surfaces disagree after a source or classification change.

cases.requirement: One-turn scale uses layered compression, batching, mission slicing, anomaly escalation, and per-repository receipts beneath one aggregate decision.
cases.failure: The system claims complete 100-repository analysis after reading only names or silently skipping unavailable proof.
